newsitem.title: USA: Cusiana sale shifts U.S. focus to regional crudes.
newsitem.headline: Cusiana sale shifts U.S. focus to regional crudes.

text.p: A sale of Cusiana crude oil has shifted the U.S. focus away from the North Sea toward regional crudes, traders said on Thursday.
Colombian state oil company Ecopetrol on Wednesday sold a 550,000 barrel cargo of the gasoline-rich grade loading September 1-10 to a U.S refiner.
The buyer paid a discount of 65 cents a barrel under West Texas Intermediate/Cushing, traders said.
The same refiner was re-offering Cusiana delivered into the U.S. Gulf, available either September 5-10 or September 10-15, asking October WTI/Cushing plus 25 cents on a cif basis.
Wednesday's Cusiana sale set the pace for the light sweet crude market even before the formal September loading program for Cusiana comes out.
An equity Cusiana seller was asking a 55-cent discount for another Cusiana cargo loading in September, traders said.
The Cusiana transaction also turned some heads away from recent talk of bringing North Sea Brent to the Gulf.
The same U.S. refiner that picked up the Cusiana cargo appeared to switch strategy on Thursday, and was no longer offering Brent into the U.S. Gulf.
Other companies and trading houses were still gauging U.S. interest, however, asking around 10 cents a barrel under WTI for first-half September arrival.
Elsewhere, a Swiss trading house this week sold a 950,000 barrel cargo of Escalante crude to China at September WTI minus $2.80 a barrel on a cost and freight basis, traders said.
This is the third cargo of Escalante that China has picked up since its first purchase in June.

Finally, trade sources said no foreign crude was delivered or redelivered into the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX) upon expiry of the August contract on Tuesday, ending a recent pattern of hefty foreign deliveries.

Recent months witnessed record deliveries of Brent, Bonny Light and Oseberg crude into the exchange. The narrowing of the trans-Atlantic arbitrage since then has diminished the possibility that more foreign crude will be delivered, at least for now, traders said.
